query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: service_quality_theme
per_column.rationale: A well-differentiated categorical axis (warm/cold/inconsistent/absent) directly serving the exploratory query on airline service. Samples map soundly to source text; the 'cold_impersonal' tag on a seat-focused complaint is a slight stretch but defensible.

per_column.name: service_decline_signal
per_column.rationale: A boolean flag adds some analytical leverage for trend/decline framing, but it is a bare true/false with modest new information beyond the theme column. Sample values (all false) are consistent with positive/neutral texts.

per_column.name: cost_cutting_perception
per_column.rationale: Distinct latent concept (perceived cost-cutting) that offers a real analytical angle, though as a rare boolean its leverage is limited. Sample values grounded and correctly false where text gives no cost-cutting cues.

per_column.name: food_quality_theme
per_column.rationale: Rich multi-valued categorization (excellent/acceptable/poor/special_meal_failure/ran_out) giving a strong grouping axis. NULLs for silent rows are appropriate. Samples map well; 'acceptable' for a food-silent review is a mild over-assertion but minor.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Useful typology of seat problems giving a fresh axis beyond the numeric Seat Comfort rating. Well grounded in samples (narrow_poor_padding, excellent_spacious) with correct NULLs for silent rows.

per_column.name: cabin_hardware_condition
per_column.rationale: Reasonable new axis on aircraft condition. However 'standard_adequate' dominates (571) and is applied to rows with no hardware mention (e.g. sample 5), suggesting a default-fill that asserts a condition the text does not support, weakening groundedness somewhat.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures how disruptions were handled, a genuinely distinct axis; 'not_applicable' correctly dominates for the many disruption-free reviews and samples are consistent.

per_column.name: ground_service_issue
per_column.rationale: Adds a ground-experience dimension absent from original columns (check-in, booking, lounge, baggage). Well grounded; 'none_mentioned' appropriately used for silent samples.

per_column.name: premium_class_value_perception
per_column.rationale: A value-perception scale is useful, but overlaps conceptually with the existing 'Value For Money' rating, and the four-way split is applied even to rows with little value discussion, producing inferred values (e.g. 'meets_expectation') that the text only weakly supports.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide a diverse, well-differentiated set of aspect-level axes (service, food, seat, cabin, disruption, ground, value) that genuinely help the open-ended exploratory query about which aspect is worth analyzing. Most are multi-valued with meaningful distributions and correct use of NULL/not_applicable for silent rows. Weaknesses: two boolean flags add limited leverage, premium_class_value_perception partly duplicates the existing Value For Money rating, and cabin_hardware_condition/value columns appear to default-fill non-null categories onto rows that are silent, a mild groundedness concern. No outright fabrications observed in the samples.
